title: ENH: add calculation of 'stress' property to ase.calculators.eam.EAM
body:
This merge request implements calculation of stresses for the EAM potential according to the virial stress definition, just like the EMT potential.
Both `stress` and `stresses` are computed in the `calculate_forces` method.
Also, `free_energy` is now set to the same value as `energy` to perform numerical stress calculations.

Added force and stress test based on the numerical force and stress calculators similar to `test/calculators/test_morse.py`.
Updated EAM docstring to mention the calculation of stress.

# Checklist

- [x] I am familiar with [ASE's contribution guidelines](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/contribute.html).
- [x] [**Doc strings**](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code) in code changed in this MR are up to date.
- [x] [**Unit tests** have been added for new or changed code.](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/tests.html)
author: UL-LIC-Floris

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
1. Division by `volume` may not work ideally for non-3D systems. Could you maybe consider the treatment like done in [`emt.py`](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/158c80304b71823ca36173560e1974e5c305ce02/ase/calculators/emt.py#L241-244) or [`morse.py`](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/158c80304b71823ca36173560e1974e5c305ce02/ase/calculators/morse.py#L150-152)?
2. According to the [docstring in `atoms.get_stresses`](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/158c80304b71823ca36173560e1974e5c305ce02/ase/atoms.py#L889-891), the definition of `stresses` in ASE is not well unified, and I am a bit hesitant to extend this feature without overviewing the present situation in ASE.
To ease the review for this MR, I would like to suggest to remove implementation of `stresses` here and focus on `stress`.
If we would like to have `stresses`, I would like to suggest to make another MR specifically for this, with summarizing the how other calculators implement this.
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer points out that dividing by `volume` may not work correctly for non-3D systems, indicating a logic/edge-case error in the stress calculation.

comments.author: UL-LIC-Floris
comments.body: Changed the volume division like in calculators you mentioned and removed the `stresses` property. I probably won't be putting in a new MR for this but just put the stresses in a local variable for now, so it can't easily be accessed again.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests two concrete changes: (1) handle non-3D systems like emt.py/morse.py, and (2) remove the `stresses` implementation and focus only on `stress`, deferring stresses to a separate MR.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.label_reasoning: This comment references the same concern as index 0 (incorrect stress/stresses calculation), pointing to the same logic error.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: References the actionable comment above, implying the same code changes apply here.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
For `stress` we should test not only `alloy` but also `eam`, `fs`, and `adp`.
In this sense, it would be more reasonable to, e.g., extend `test_eam_run.py::test_read_potential` rather than this `test_eam`, which tests if `EAM` can handle a user-defined potential.
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer is suggesting that the test should be placed in a different test file/function to better match the existing test organization and cover all relevant potential types (eam, fs, adp).

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests extending test coverage to include eam, fs, and adp formats, and suggests using a different test file.
